features.feature_value: Favored posts that were not insulting and aimed to contribute to healthy conversation; avoided/penalized crudeness/insults
features.evidence_span: ones that weren't insulting others off the bat
features.rationale: The participant explicitly ties influence/choice to whether the posts insulted others and promoted healthy conversation.

features.feature_value: Allowed most posts as healthy discourse, but rejected when there was name calling/profanity or extreme personal accusations (e.g., calling Trump a 'cancer')
features.evidence_span: when there was name calling, profanity or for instance accusing President Trump as being "...a cancer..."
features.rationale: They describe a concrete threshold (respectful debating) that fails specifically for profanity/name-calling/harsh personal labels.

features.feature_value: Preferred open-ended, discussion-suitable prompts; viewed some statements as dead ends/unfollowable, while pure insults were unnecessary and not tied to political topics
features.evidence_span: dead ends and cannot follow up on a proper discussion
features.rationale: They contrast posts by whether they invite proper discussion (open-ended) versus being dead ends or merely insults.

features.feature_value: Used a risk/effect lens: considered whether the posts could cause further harm and whether there was evidence supporting the ideas
features.evidence_span: if further harm might be produced by either of the posts
features.rationale: They state their criteria directly as harm potential and presence of evidence.

features.feature_value: Tried to judge impartially and avoid bias
features.evidence_span: I just tried to be fair, not biased.
features.rationale: The reflection explicitly describes an impartiality goal as their approach.

features.feature_value: Emphasized freedom of speech but treated bad-mouthing other parties as unhelpful for addressing real national problems
features.evidence_span: bad mouthing other parties doesn't help
features.rationale: They articulate a balancing principle: allow speech broadly, but disfavor degrading attacks aimed at parties.

features.feature_value: Believed misunderstanding between sides is inevitable, implying limited expectation that pairing/seeing both would resolve conflict
features.evidence_span: There is always a lack of understanding on each side
features.rationale: They express a generalized belief about persistent misunderstanding, shaping their stance toward the task.

features.feature_value: Viewed showing both viewpoints as essential to understanding each side and reaching conclusions; supports free speech in general
features.evidence_span: open discussion showing both viewpoints is essential
features.rationale: They explicitly justify influence via the value of seeing both sides for understanding and decision-making.
